SOURCE-ASSISTED READING AND COMPARISON, 22 September 2026

Base: review-2026-09-22-image-only, unchanged. This review read that record and the former F-hcpv report before inspecting manuscript crops and the Acta Sanctorum comparison text. It is source-assisted, not independent or human palaeographic verification. Exact model identifier unavailable.

Inputs: original packet image-001.png; cached manuscript column crops h0a.jpg, h0b.jpg, h1a.jpg, h1b.jpg, h2a.jpg, h2b.jpg; earlier report and frozen record; Heiligenlexikon Acta Sanctorum September VIII index; the downloaded 30 September HTML edition transcription and a locally extracted plain-text version. No printed edition facsimile, Armenian edition, or independent Greek collation was inspected.

The column crops correspond, according to cached provenance, to image0077 (h0a/b), image0079 (h1a/b), image0078 (h2a/b). Original native crop origin/scale was not independently recovered. Lines below are physical lines counted from each column crop's top. They are selected, not a complete transcript. The packet's seven rows overlap h0a rows1–7 and must not be counted again. Parentheses propose expansions, ? marks doubt, and [illegible] leaves unresolved image text.

Other inspected context: h0a's Constantine encomium; h0b's reception by Silvester; h1a's exchange of stories, Constantine's leprosy and baptism by Silvester, friendship and return; h1b's council convening; h2a's vesting/burial and miracles; h2b's final doxology and line filler. No full new transcription of these areas is supplied. The burial place remains unresolved rather than normalized to Valarsapath.

Actual primary comparison:
https://www.heiligenlexikon.de/ActaSanctorum/30.September.html
Acta Sanctorum Sept. VIII, Gregory: longer Greek Vita and its Latin translation, CAPUT XV, §§163–173 (the web transcription's heading is XV). Read Latin §§163–173 and pertinent editorial notes, especially the discussion of Eusebius/Silvester and death traditions. Greek text was visible during extraction, but not separately collated. Also read Vita altera, headed Auctore anonymo / Ex codice Ms. bibliothecae Barberinae / BHL3664, §§38–43; the closing §§41–43 were compared with the manuscript ending. Evidence is the site's HTML transcription of the edition, not a facsimile inspection.

The longer Vita's Latin translation §§165–166 has the diagnostic retinue: Norsireorum, Assyriae, Aruastarum, Masachi, Angelitae, crowning Aspet, Macitarum, Synistarum, Restunitarum, Sapianarum, Pascapeteorum; seventy thousand soldiers; departure from Ararat and Valarsapat; journey by land and sea to Italy/Rome. The manuscript shares this distinctive assemblage and order with altered names, compression and wording. This is substantial narrative-family evidence, not sustained identity of the Latin text. In §166 the receiving churchman is Eusebius, whereas the manuscript has Silvester and adds Constantine's leprosy/baptism story. The editorial note discusses the Silvester tradition; it does not identify the manuscript recension.

A separate location, §169, sends Arostaces to Nicaea and brings him back with its canons to the king and Gregory; the manuscript's chapter IV has the same linked sequence with Erostacius/Erostacis but substantially different prose and an expanded council assembly. Longer Vita §170 emphasizes continued pastoral vigilance and not giving sleep to the eyes, comparable to h2a rows1–5, but its §§171–173 do not give the manuscript's detailed funeral and royal coda.

BHL3664 Vita altera §§41–43 instead moves through Gregory's withdrawal, Teridacius's visits/penitence, written sermons and a generic peaceful death, ending with a feast date and doxology. The manuscript's summons to his son, king, wife and sister, testament, burial in a named city with church/miracles, and final pig/angel comparison for the king are not the ending printed there. This is a real scoped textual comparison, replacing the old inaccessible-source limitation. It does not exclude every witness or recension attached to BHL3664, and does not establish that the manuscript text is unedited.

Result: Partial; medium confidence for a substantial diagnostic narrative connection to the longer Agathangelos tradition. Exact Latin work/recension and attribution remain unresolved. Confidence applies to the retinue-plus-journey-and-council connection, not Latin verbal identity or historical authorship. The additional passages were already exposed in the old report, so no held-out check is claimed. No dating, Greek-intermediary, common-manuscript, quire, missing-leaf-count or witness-novelty conclusion follows from these checks. Fresh comparison with F-0kql was not performed by this reviewer.
